LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 TYPES OF SENTENCES: INTERROGATIVE SENTENCES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How do we ask questions? 2. How do we answer questions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. Identify interrogative sentences and question tags from a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. Use interrogative sentences and question tags in varied contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. Appreciate the role of correctly framed questions in communication. • Read a text online or offline on varied topics including tourist attraction sites in Africa Adjust light intensity when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties. • Identify interrogative sentences such as WH- questions, Yes/ No questions and alternative questions. • Identify question tags from a given text and practise asking and answering them • Form interrogatives and tag questions and display them on a graphic organiser, with peers, • Use interrogatives in a role play relevant to the theme of tourism in Africa • Read a dialogue featuring interrogatives and tag questions, with peers, 1. How do we ask questions? 2. How do we answer questions? 136 • Search the internet for more examples of question tags and interrogatives.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration is developed as the learner accomplishes different tasks while dramatising and recording

sections of the short story that reflect real life experiences.

• Self- efficacy is sharpened as the learner documents successes achieved while constructing different types of interrogatives.

Values:
Respect is emphasised as learners appreciate others while engaging in a dialogue featuring interrogative sentences and question

tags.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Problem Solving is promoted as learners ask and answer questions on tourism in Africa.

Link to other subjects:

Social Studies, Religious Education and Mathematics involve asking and answering questions.
